title: Choose NexaMind's visual world
question: The roll assigned Sprint Wall. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Sprint Wall
options.lineage: the team wall of index cards and sticky notes every startup sprint runs on
options.thesis: The whole team's work pinned to one wall: every doc, chat, meeting and task is a card with a coloured tab.
materials: index-card stock with a red header rule
options.viewport: Ink-black rail, chalk-white wall; the dashboard is a pinned board of cards, each topped by its feature's sticky tab, every panel heading underlined by the index card's red rule.
options.risk: Turns toy-like if sticky colours flood big areas; they stay on tabs, tags and the Solo/Group switch.

raised.raise: States stamp, never vanish: approved minutes and done tasks carry a stamped state.
One baseline, one scale: every panel sits on a shared 4px grid with even card heights per row.
One numeric voice: every count, time and amount set in tabular figures.
Columns thin but never merge: rail, panel and work area hold until the phone layout.

options.label: Braun Functional
options.thesis: A calm instrument for the working day: matte grey, graphite and one orange signal.
options.viewport: Graphite rail, warm grey ground, white panels with soft radii; one orange control carries the primary action.
options.risk: Familiar: close to many calm dev tools, and the orange reads as a warning if it spreads.

options.label: Workspace Transit Map
options.thesis: Docs, chat, meetings, tasks and code run as coloured lines; where work connects, an interchange blooms.
options.viewport: Midnight rail, porcelain work area; the dashboard header is a small network of today's activity with interchanges.
options.case: Fuses well: links between features become interchanges, so it holds clarity; teams don't picture their work as a metro, so it loses identification.
options.risk: The diagram must come from real link data, or it is decoration.

options.label: One-Screen Mosaic
options.thesis: Every part of the workspace tiled on one screen in ruled modules with small red tabs.
options.viewport: A persistent nav rail and a mosaic of ruled modules: docs, chat, meetings, tasks and repos all visible at once.
options.case: Holds clarity, since everything really is in one place on one screen; loses identification with small Western dev teams.
options.risk: Overwhelms newcomers, and small type tires the eyes over a working day.

options.label: Ticket Wallet
options.thesis: Each workflow as a coupon book that tears off leg by leg.
options.viewport: Coupon stack per meeting: transcript, minutes, tasks as legs.
options.case: Fuses poorly: teams don't see their work as travel; the coupon model hides the connected workspace.
options.risk: Pure costume on a working screen.
options.kept: States that stamp instead of disappearing.

options.label: Dance Score
options.thesis: Work read upward along a centre staff, length as duration.
options.viewport: A vertical staff of the day's events.
options.case: Fuses poorly on both axes: unfamiliar notation and no link to how teams work.
options.kept: A column layout that thins but never merges.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: Each project shown as plates of one plant through its seasons.
options.viewport: Project stages as fixed-scale plates on one baseline.
options.case: Fuses poorly: lovely, but neither a dev team's world nor a clearer product.
options.risk: Cream and serif: the default look every model ships.
options.kept: Fixed scale and one shared baseline across panels.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: The workspace as a black-and-white data field.
options.case: Fuses poorly: harsh for daily work and hides the content.
options.risk: Strobing and pure contrast fatigue people within an hour.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What team workspaces like Linear and Notion ship, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Grey sidebar, white canvas, compact lists and one accent colour.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
